frontmatter_description: Diagnose whether one goal is a higher-level aim, a subgoal, or a local step within a goal structure.
title: Goal Hierarchy
use_when: Use when the question asks whether a goal is long-term, short-term, or local relative to another goal.
Use when you need to identify which stated goal is a means to a higher goal and which is the end goal.
Use when the task is to map the hierarchy among goals without choosing between them.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the question asks which goal will win, which desire is stronger, or what the character will choose.
Do not use when the main issue is preference, intention, action prediction, or commitment priority.
Do not use when the scene is about resolving conflict between goals rather than classifying their levels.
decision_variable: which goal is superordinate versus subordinate
trigger_checklist: There are two or more goals, plans, or aims mentioned.
The question asks for level, nesting, or means-end relation.
One goal appears to support another goal or larger purpose.
No direct choice between competing goals is required.
workflow: List every stated goal, plan, or objective.
Ask whether one goal serves another goal or stands as the final aim.
Classify each goal as long-term, short-term, or local.
Answer with the hierarchy only, not with the chosen action.

special_case.title: Subgoal inside a plan
special_case.rule: If a small action is part of a larger plan, treat it as a local or short-term goal only when the question asks for level, not when it asks which action will happen next.

worked_example.scene: A student studies for a quiz so that she can pass the class.
worked_example.question: Which goal is higher-level?
worked_example.answer_logic: Passing the class is the higher-level goal; studying for the quiz is the subordinate goal that serves it.

boundary_exit_rule: Exit to micro-25 Goal-Conflict Arbitration if the question asks which goal wins or is weighted higher.
Exit to micro-24 Commitment Priority if a binding promise, plan, or schedule sets the priority.
Exit to micro-23 Action Prediction if the scene requires predicting the next action from goals.
Exit to micro-22 Intention Recognition if the issue is inferring the immediate purpose behind a current behavior.
Exit to micro-19 or micro-20 if the issue is mental-state reading of the character's own or another person's desire or preference.

references.route_signal: Use this micro unit when a case asks how goals are nested or whether a goal is a means versus an end.
hard_boundary: The target is the means-end structure among goals, not which goal wins (that is micro-25).
The target is structural level, not the choice forced by a binding promise or schedule (that is micro-24).
The target is hierarchy, not the immediate purpose of a present behavior (that is micro-22).
The target is goal nesting, not the next observable action (that is micro-23).
shortcut_to_avoid: Do not treat the goal that gets mentioned first as the higher-level goal.
Do not infer hierarchy from which goal feels more important unless the relation is explicitly asked.
Do not use the final action as evidence of the top-level goal without checking the stated plan structure.
common_failure_modes: Confusing a subtask with the main objective.
Answering which goal the character will pursue instead of which goal is higher-level.
Equating short-term with low value and long-term with preference without textual support.
Merging goal hierarchy with intention or action prediction.

minimal_pair.case: A person buys ingredients so he can make dinner for his family.
minimal_pair.why_it_matches: The question can ask which goal is the higher-level aim, with buying ingredients as a subgoal.

minimal_pair.case: A girl writes a reminder so she will not forget the meeting.
minimal_pair.why_it_matches: The reminder is a local means; not forgetting the meeting is the broader goal.

boundary_stress_test: If two goals compete, do not rank them here; route to preference or commitment.
If the story asks what the person will do next, do not answer hierarchy.
If the only clue is that one goal happens earlier in time, that is not enough to prove it is higher-level.
references.generalization_note: Use this unit only for means-end structure among goals; it does not decide choice, value, or behavior.

validation_seed.positive_pattern: One goal is clearly a step or instrument for another goal, and the question asks which is higher-level.
validation_seed.near_miss_pattern: Two goals are mentioned and the question asks which one the character will choose.
validation_seed.boundary_pattern: The character has conflicting wants, but the question asks for the more important one.

notes: This unit supports diagnosis inside broader goal-action scenes, but only for hierarchy, not selection.
Keep the answer structural: superordinate goal, subordinate goal, or local step.
If the scene asks why an action was done, route to intention recognition instead.
core_question: Distinguish long-term, short-term, and local goals
